A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same future frame synthesis survey, with corresponding core sections. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison across all 25 and 37 pages. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 2.2 explicitly states that the authors calculate missing mean or median dataset statistics, reported in Table 1. This constitutes original descriptive data analysis, although the model-performance findings are attributed to other studies.

after.justification: Section 2.4 retains the authors' estimation of missing dataset statistics, and the expanded Table 1 reports descriptive outcomes. Original data analysis therefore remains present without an author-conducted model benchmark.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an implemented synthesis algorithm or model. v6 expands descriptions of surveyed architectures; its additional multimodal equation formalizes the task rather than introducing a new method.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds surveyed datasets, including sky and facial-video collections, but neither version reports conducting model training or evaluation on these datasets. The catalogue expansion does not establish changed experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed algorithm. The new method tables summarize publications and their ideas, without establishing an evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: v6 discusses VBench, FVMD, and VBench-2.0 but does not apply them in an evaluation. The stated mean/median approach to missing dataset statistics remains unchanged, with no revised experimental splits, budgets, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version reports its own ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or error analyses. v6's Figure 1 illustrates dataset examples; the additional discussions summarize cited research.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same mean and median reporting conventions. Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; added descriptive values do not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds descriptive results, including mean clip lengths of 408 frames for MSR-VTT and 245 for QST. The matched OpenDV-YouTube/OpenDV-2K entry changes from 100,000+ mean frames to 'variable.' Section 5.1 also adds literature-attributed capability findings, without a comparable rerun demonstrating performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1) and (2) replace the erroneous multiplication of observed frames by a conditional probability with sampling from a conditional distribution. New Equation (3) formalizes joint prediction of future frames and multimodal information. These are localized mathematical corrections and extensions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the stochasticity-based taxonomy, emphasis on generative synthesis, integration of prediction and generation, and two future research directions. The added abstract statement about future exploration was already represented in v5's conclusion.

C2.justification: v6 adds substantive explanations of overlapping stochastic and generative paradigms in Sections 2.2 and 4, physical and contextual validity in evaluation in Section 2.3, and improving generation without increasing parameter counts in Section 5.1. It also expands application interpretations and adds a broader-impact discussion.

D1.justification: New Table 5 and Section 5.1 document model sizes and reported release availability for surveyed resources, including HunyuanVideo at 13B parameters and both Step-Video models at 30B. These additions provide resource information without documenting a changed implementation by the survey authors.

R1.justification: v6 substantially expands coverage of foundational architectures, flow matching, Gaussian motion representations, video-specific evaluation, recent large video generators, and robotics pretraining. These substantive additions go beyond publication updates and renamings of retained works such as SV2P and Multi-Scale AdvGDL.

P1.justification: Prose is extensively rewritten throughout. Section 2 gains 'Paradigms and Architectures,' reorganizes challenges into numbered subsections, and moves datasets to Section 2.4. Other changes include reorganized method discussions, revised terminology, a broader-impact paragraph, and authorship and affiliation edits.

P2.justification: v6 adds the dataset illustration in Figure 1 and Tables 2–5, substantially changing the presentation of the survey. Tables 2–4 organize both retained and newly discussed literature. Table 1 is expanded, reordered, and relocated, while the underlying page style remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v5's predominantly prose-based overview, v6 improves navigation, explains the taxonomy more explicitly, incorporates video-specific evaluation research, and corrects the conditional-probability formulation. These gains are tempered by new summary inconsistencies: Table 4 describes Video Transformer as a classification method, whereas Section 5.2 describes autoregressive video generation. The net improvement is useful but qualified.
